text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonia's total foreign debt is $1.1 billion. Over half of its obligations are owed to the Paris and London clubs of creditors.
- Head of Macedonian delegation on talks about legal succession of former Yugoslavia, Tahir Kadriu, said "a mimimum agreement is better than endless arbitration".

- All political parties will run cadidates for mayors of new municipalities throughout Macedonia. The opposition coalition IMRO-DPMNY, Democratic Party and MAAK-Conservative party at convention in Skopje say victory at local level will bring victory in 1998 parliamentary elections.
- A 13-year old boy murdered and butchered his mother and brother in Struga on Friday morning, police from the town reported. The investigative judge says "the reason was a family fight".

- A Council of Europe report says Macedonian media are under strong state control. Government sources are rejecting this opinion with the argument there are 320 publications in Macedonia "which are very hard to control." -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201196
